reader.requirement: For an indexed file in sequential access mode the REWRITE replaces the record named by the prime record key, which must equal the prime key of the last record read; any other value is refused with the invalid key condition (I-O status 21) and nothing is replaced.

reader.notes: IndexedConnector#Rewrite tests sequential access alone (Access == Sequential) and compares the record's prime key with _lastReadPrime under the prime key's order, returning 21 before anything changes. Probes cover changed-to-existing, changed-to-absent, elementary and group record-names, REWRITE FROM.

refuter.evidence: Attack: in 1985 the prime key's order is the NATIVE collating sequence, never the program collating sequence (§1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3), so 'equal to the prime key of the last record read' must be judged natively. q1col.cob (refute-1985-098/q1col-001): PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE IS ALF, ALPHABET ALF IS "A" ALSO "a" "B" ALSO "b" (IF "AB01" = "ab01" prints PCS EQUAL); sequential READ AB01, key changed to ab01, REWRITE -> C1 IK 21, file unchanged (CHK AB01DATA01). Code: IndexedConnector#Rewrite compares under _orders.Prime, which FileControlBinder#ResolveFileCollating leaves native when no file COLLATING clause is written ('no clause -> native'). q2alt.cob A1: READ after START on a duplicates alternate (READ status 02) then REWRITE same prime -> 00. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.6.4 GR13  (4.6.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR13'; 'OK  §1985:IX.2.3.4 GR3  (2.3.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR3'.
